changes: Expose the existing single-row materialization planner through the generic plan contract; owned single-row materialization uses it too.
Select batch scalar predicate workspace when its planned admission uses at most half current available capacity; otherwise evaluate one admitted row at a time.
Keep selection and output ownership unchanged; no user tuning required.

validation.fixture: 256 Parquet rows with 4096-code-unit Unicode partition text and scalar LIKE operate within a 128 KiB pool.

limitations: Local microbenchmark measures materialization and disposal, not cloud I/O or complete queries.
Single-row processing costs more CPU; the headroom rule is a conservative heuristic, not a measured runtime throughput optimizer.
Planner traversal bookkeeping and full query allocation coverage remain under audit.
Final release gates and production whole-heap bounds remain unproven.
